metadata.title: Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate

nodes.name: Neural Machine Translation
nodes.statement: Given a source sentence $\mathbf{x}$, find a target sentence $\mathbf{y}^* = \arg\max_{\mathbf{y}} p(\mathbf{y} \mid \mathbf{x})$ where $p(\mathbf{y} \mid \mathbf{x})$ is parameterized by a neural network trained on a parallel corpus.
nodes.statement_clean: Translate sentence x to sentence y by maximizing a learned conditional probability p(y|x) parameterized by a neural network.

nodes.name: RNN Encoder--Decoder
nodes.statement: A model in which an encoder RNN reads a source sequence $\mathbf{x} = (x_1, \dots, x_{T_x})$ and produces a fixed-length context vector $c = q(\{h_1, \dots, h_{T_x}\})$ from hidden states $h_t = f(x_t, h_{t-1})$; a decoder RNN then defines $p(\mathbf{y}) = \prod_t p(y_t \mid y_1, \dots, y_{t-1}, c)$.
nodes.statement_clean: An encoder RNN compresses the source sentence into a single fixed-length vector, which a decoder RNN unrolls into the target sentence.
nodes.origin_citation: Cho et al. 2014; Sutskever et al. 2014

nodes.name: Annotation
nodes.statement: An annotation $h_j = [\overrightarrow{h}_j^\top ; \overleftarrow{h}_j^\top]^\top$ is the concatenation of the forward and backward hidden states of a bidirectional RNN at position $j$, summarising both preceding and following context around source word $x_j$.
nodes.statement_clean: A per-source-position vector that summarizes the whole input sequence with a strong focus on the words around position j.

nodes.name: Bidirectional RNN (BiRNN)
nodes.statement: A pair of RNNs consisting of a forward RNN $\overrightarrow{f}$ that reads $x_1, \dots, x_{T_x}$ producing $(\overrightarrow{h}_1, \dots, \overrightarrow{h}_{T_x})$ and a backward RNN $\overleftarrow{f}$ reading $x_{T_x}, \dots, x_1$ producing $(\overleftarrow{h}_1, \dots, \overleftarrow{h}_{T_x})$.
nodes.statement_clean: An encoder consisting of one RNN that reads forward and another that reads backward over the input.

nodes.name: Alignment model
nodes.statement: A feedforward neural network $a(s_{i-1}, h_j) = v_a^\top \tanh(W_a s_{i-1} + U_a h_j)$ producing a scalar score $e_{ij}$ that measures how well source position $j$ matches target position $i$; jointly trained with the rest of the system.
nodes.statement_clean: A small MLP that scores each source annotation against the previous decoder state to produce alignment energies.

nodes.name: Soft alignment / attention weights
nodes.statement: A probability distribution $\alpha_{ij} = \dfrac{\exp(e_{ij})}{\sum_{k=1}^{T_x} \exp(e_{ik})}$ over source positions for each target position $i$, interpreted as the probability that target word $y_i$ is aligned to source word $x_j$.
nodes.statement_clean: Softmax-normalized alignment scores giving a probability over source positions for each target word.

nodes.name: Context vector
nodes.statement: Per-target-position context $c_i = \sum_{j=1}^{T_x} \alpha_{ij} h_j$ — the expected annotation under the soft-alignment distribution $\alpha_{i\cdot}$.
nodes.statement_clean: A per-step weighted sum of source annotations under the attention distribution.

nodes.name: Gated hidden unit
nodes.statement: An RNN unit with state update $s_i = (1 - z_i) \circ s_{i-1} + z_i \circ \tilde{s}_i$, where $\tilde{s}_i = \tanh(W e(y_{i-1}) + U[r_i \circ s_{i-1}] + C c_i)$, $z_i = \sigma(W_z e(y_{i-1}) + U_z s_{i-1} + C_z c_i)$, $r_i = \sigma(W_r e(y_{i-1}) + U_r s_{i-1} + C_r c_i)$.
nodes.statement_clean: An RNN unit with multiplicative update and reset gates, similar in spirit to LSTM, used in place of plain tanh.

nodes.name: Maxout deep output layer
nodes.statement: Output probability $p(y_i \mid s_i, y_{i-1}, c_i) \propto \exp(y_i^\top W_o t_i)$ where $t_i = [\max\{\tilde{t}_{i,2j-1}, \tilde{t}_{i,2j}\}]_{j=1,\dots,l}$ and $\tilde{t}_i = U_o s_{i-1} + V_o E y_{i-1} + C_o c_i$.
nodes.statement_clean: A deep output layer with a single maxout hidden layer that produces softmax probabilities over the target vocabulary.

nodes.name: Encoder forward state recurrence
nodes.statement: $h_t = f(x_t, h_{t-1})$ — the hidden state at time $t$ for an encoder RNN with arbitrary nonlinear $f$.

nodes.name: Decoder factorization
nodes.statement: $p(\mathbf{y}) = \prod_{t=1}^{T_y} p(y_t \mid \{y_1, \dots, y_{t-1}\}, c)$ with $p(y_t \mid \{y_1, \dots, y_{t-1}\}, c) = g(y_{t-1}, s_t, c)$.

nodes.name: Per-target conditional with context $c_i$
nodes.statement: $p(y_i \mid y_1, \dots, y_{i-1}, \mathbf{x}) = g(y_{i-1}, s_i, c_i)$ where $s_i = f(s_{i-1}, y_{i-1}, c_i)$ and $c_i$ is a target-position-dependent context vector.

nodes.name: Context vector formula
nodes.statement: $c_i = \sum_{j=1}^{T_x} \alpha_{ij} h_j$.

nodes.name: Attention softmax
nodes.statement: $\alpha_{ij} = \dfrac{\exp(e_{ij})}{\sum_{k=1}^{T_x} \exp(e_{ik})}$, $e_{ij} = a(s_{i-1}, h_j)$.

nodes.name: RNNsearch (jointly aligning and translating decoder)
nodes.statement: Encode the source with a BiRNN to obtain annotations $(h_1, \dots, h_{T_x})$; at each decoding step compute soft-alignment weights $\alpha_{ij}$, the context $c_i = \sum_j \alpha_{ij} h_j$, the new hidden state $s_i = f(s_{i-1}, y_{i-1}, c_i)$, and the output distribution $p(y_i \mid \cdot) \propto \exp(y_i^\top W_o t_i)$.
input: Trained encoder weights $\overrightarrow{W}, \overrightarrow{U}, \overleftarrow{W}, \overleftarrow{U}, \overline{E}$ and decoder weights $W, U, C, W_z, U_z, C_z, W_r, U_r, C_r, W_a, U_a, v_a, W_o, U_o, V_o, C_o, E$

nodes.name: Minibatch SGD with Adadelta and length-bucketed minibatches
nodes.statement: Train the model parameters with stochastic gradient descent using Adadelta ($\epsilon = 10^{-6}, \rho = 0.95$), gradient $L_2$-norm clipped at $1$, on minibatches of $80$ sentences pre-sorted by length every 20 updates.
input: Initial parameters (recurrent matrices random orthogonal; $W_a, U_a$ Gaussian $(0, 0.001^2)$; others Gaussian $(0, 0.01^2)$)
output: Trained parameters of the RNNsearch (or RNNencdec) model

nodes.name: Beam search decoding
nodes.statement: After training, generate a translation by beam search that approximately maximizes the conditional probability $p(\mathbf{y} \mid \mathbf{x})$ under the trained model.

nodes.name: Encode source with bidirectional RNN
nodes.statement: Compute forward states $\overrightarrow{h}_i$ from $x_1$ to $x_{T_x}$ and backward states $\overleftarrow{h}_i$ from $x_{T_x}$ to $x_1$ using gated hidden units; concatenate to form annotations $h_i = [\overrightarrow{h}_i^\top; \overleftarrow{h}_i^\top]^\top$.

nodes.name: Initialize decoder state
nodes.statement: Set $s_0 = \tanh(W_s \overleftarrow{h}_1)$ from the first backward annotation.

nodes.name: Generate target words (decoding loop)
nodes.statement: For $i = 1, 2, \dots$: compute energies $e_{ij} = v_a^\top \tanh(W_a s_{i-1} + U_a h_j)$ for all $j$, softmax to get $\alpha_{ij}$, compute $c_i = \sum_j \alpha_{ij} h_j$, update $s_i = f(s_{i-1}, y_{i-1}, c_i)$ via the gated unit, and sample/score $y_i$ via the maxout deep output. Repeat until end-of-sentence.

nodes.name: Return translation and alignment matrix
nodes.statement: Return the generated target sequence $\mathbf{y} = (y_1, \dots, y_{T_y})$ together with the alignment matrix $[\alpha_{ij}]$.

nodes.name: Initialize parameters
nodes.statement: Initialize recurrent matrices ($U, U_z, U_r, \overrightarrow{U}, \overrightarrow{U}_z, \overrightarrow{U}_r, \overleftarrow{U}, \overleftarrow{U}_z, \overleftarrow{U}_r$) as random orthogonal matrices; sample $W_a, U_a$ from $\mathcal{N}(0, 0.001^2)$; sample other weights from $\mathcal{N}(0, 0.01^2)$; zero biases and $V_a$.

nodes.name: Sort and bucket minibatches
nodes.statement: Every 20 updates, retrieve 1600 sentence pairs, sort by length, and split into 20 minibatches of 80 to minimize wasted padding computation.

nodes.name: SGD update with Adadelta and gradient clipping
nodes.statement: For each minibatch, compute the gradient of $-\log p(\mathbf{y} \mid \mathbf{x})$, clip its $L_2$ norm to $1$, and apply an Adadelta update ($\epsilon = 10^{-6}, \rho = 0.95$). Loop until validation log-likelihood stops improving.

nodes.name: BLEU vs sentence length on WMT'14 En--Fr
nodes.statement: On WMT'14 English-to-French test set, RNNsearch-50 achieves BLEU $26.75$ overall and $34.16$ on sentences with no UNK; RNNencdec-50 achieves only $17.82$ / $26.71$. RNNencdec degrades sharply with length while RNNsearch-50 remains essentially flat for sentences of length $\geq 50$.

nodes.name: Sample alignment matrices (Fig. 3)
nodes.statement: Visualisation of $\alpha_{ij}$ for four English--French sentence pairs: alignments are largely monotonic with diagonal mass, but show non-monotonic jumps for adjective--noun reorderings (e.g. [European Economic Area] $\to$ [zone \'economique europ\'eenne]).

nodes.name: Long-sentence translation: ``admitting privilege''
nodes.statement: RNNencdec-50 deviates after [a medical center] (replaces [based on his status as a health care worker at a hospital] with [en fonction de son \'etat de sant\'e]); RNNsearch-50 produces a faithful French translation preserving the full meaning.

nodes.name: Long-sentence translation: ``Disney's efforts''
nodes.statement: RNNencdec-50 deviates after $\approx 30$ generated words and omits the closing quote; RNNsearch-50 produces a correct, complete French translation including the closing quotation mark.

nodes.name: Fixed-length-vector bottleneck conjecture
nodes.statement: The authors conjecture that compressing a whole source sentence into a single fixed-length vector is the bottleneck limiting the basic encoder--decoder, especially on long sentences — the motivation for introducing per-step context vectors.

nodes.name: Soft alignment as expected annotation
nodes.statement: The weighted sum $c_i = \sum_j \alpha_{ij} h_j$ can be read as the expected annotation under a distribution $\alpha_{i\cdot}$ over alignments — making attention a marginalisation over alignment, not a latent variable to be inferred.

nodes.name: Reduction to RNN Encoder--Decoder
nodes.statement: Fixing $c_i = \overrightarrow{h}_{T_x}$ (i.e. ignoring the alignment model) reduces the proposed model to the standard RNN Encoder--Decoder of Cho et al. 2014.

nodes.name: Computational cost of attention
nodes.statement: The alignment model is evaluated $T_x \times T_y$ times per sentence pair; $U_a h_j$ does not depend on $i$ and can be pre-computed. This $O(T_x T_y)$ scaling is acceptable for translation (15--40 word sentences) but may limit applicability to longer-sequence tasks.

nodes.name: Difference from Graves 2013 monotonic attention
nodes.statement: Graves's handwriting-synthesis attention uses a mixture of Gaussian kernels with monotonically increasing centres; this is too restrictive for translation, which requires (long-distance) reordering.

nodes.name: Soft vs hard alignment for ``the man''
nodes.statement: The French determiner [le/la/les/l'] depends on the following noun, so any hard alignment of [the] is locally ambiguous; soft alignment lets the model attend simultaneously to [the] and [man] and choose [l'] correctly.
